title: Positive cosine and sine operators
subtitle: G2 lecture 046000 · expanded mathematical companion
adaptation: Standalone companion adapted from the source spoken lecture and display-only mathematics appendix. Explicit hypotheses, stepwise proofs, worked examples, and local vector diagrams; no narration edits.

slides.title: An angle becomes an operator
slides.lead: For a single pair of lines, cosine measures retained length and sine measures perpendicular loss.
body: For two closed subspaces U and V, there can be many independent principal angles. Orthogonal projections P and Q encode all of them without choosing principal vectors or even assuming a discrete spectrum.
We seek positive operators that behave like cosine and sine on each principal plane. Their construction comes from the projection difference and the positive functional calculus.
slides.takeaway: The pair (P,Q) contains a full operator-valued angle description.
slides.eyebrow: G2 · 046000 · An angle becomes an operator

slides.title: The one-angle model
slides.lead: Place U on the horizontal axis and let V be a line tilted by an angle θ between zero and ninety degrees.
body: The component of a unit vector in U that lies along V has norm cos θ. The component perpendicular to V has norm sin θ. These are two orthogonal parts of the same vector.
A matrix of two projections makes this quantitative: the norm of their difference equals sin θ. This is the scalar identity the ambient sine operator will reproduce on each principal block.
slides.takeaway: Projection difference measures the sine of an angle between lines.

slides.title: Define the positive sine and cosine
slides.lead: Let D=P−Q. The square D² is positive and bounded by the identity.
body: Taking positive square roots gives S=|D| and C=(I−D²)^{1/2}. Since 0≤D²≤I, both square roots are defined and positive. They are functions of the same self-adjoint operator.
On a principal plane with angle θ, S acts by sin θ and C by cos θ. On an exact common direction the values are 0 and 1; on a crossed right-angle defect they are 1 and 0.
slides.takeaway: The sine and cosine operators are canonical positive functions of P−Q.
slides.eyebrow: G2 · 046000 · Define the positive sine and cosine

slides.title: An operator Pythagorean identity
slides.lead: The basic trigonometric identity holds as an exact operator equality.
body: By construction S²=D² and C²=I−D². Adding the two equations gives S²+C²=I. Since both are functions of D², S and C commute.
This is more than a mnemonic: it means the same spectral decomposition can be used for both. Each singular-angle direction receives complementary cosine and sine factors.
slides.takeaway: The operator sine and cosine share one positive spectral geometry.

slides.title: Why they preserve each side of the pair
slides.lead: Although P and Q need not commute, D² commutes with both of them.
body: Expand the square: D²=P+Q−PQ−QP. Direct multiplication and P²=P, Q²=Q show PD²=D²P and QD²=D²Q.
Therefore every continuous function of D², including S and C, also commutes with P and Q. The same positive angle operators act compatibly on U, U⊥, V, and V⊥.
slides.takeaway: Projection algebra forces the positive angle functions to respect both subspaces.
slides.eyebrow: G2 · 046000 · Why they preserve each side of the pair

slides.title: Cosine seen from within U
slides.lead: For x in U, the projection Qx is the part of x retained by V.
body: Because Px=x and Q is orthogonal, the squared retained length is ⟨Qx,x⟩=⟨PQP x,x⟩. The compression PQP on U is positive and has spectral values cos² θ.
The complementary squared escape into V⊥ is ⟨(I−Q)x,x⟩. This gives the same Pythagorean decomposition directly from projections and makes the cross-Gram interpretation visible.
slides.takeaway: The positive compression PQP records squared cosines on the source subspace.
slides.eyebrow: G2 · 046000 · Cosine seen from within U

slides.title: Three endpoint behaviors
slides.lead: Exact overlap and exact orthogonality are distinguished by the spectrum, not by the appearance of a diagram.
body: If x lies in U∩V, then Px=Qx=x, so Sx=0 and Cx=x. If x lies in U∩V⊥, then Px=x and Qx=0, so Sx=x and Cx=0.

On a generic principal plane with angle strictly between zero and ninety degrees, both factors are positive. In infinite dimensions, C may still have values approaching zero without ever having a kernel.
slides.takeaway: Zero, interior, and right-angle spectral behaviors must remain distinct.

slides.title: From sine to the angle operator
slides.lead: A positive contraction S supports the functional calculus function arcsine.
body: Define Θ=arcsin S by applying arcsine to the spectrum of S, which lies in [0,1]. Then S=sin Θ and C=cos Θ, where Θ is positive with spectrum in [0,π/2].
This construction also handles continuous angle spectra. No enumeration of principal vectors is necessary, so it provides an ambient definition even when infinitely many angles accumulate.
slides.takeaway: Functional calculus converts operator sine values into a canonical nonnegative angle operator.
slides.eyebrow: G2 · 046000 · From sine to the angle operator

slides.title: A diagonal-plane example
slides.lead: A direct sum of two independent principal planes has two independently chosen angles.
body: Let each plane carry two lines meeting at θ₁ and θ₂. Then the projection difference acts on the first block with sine magnitude sin θ₁ and on the second with sin θ₂.
Consequently the operator norm of P−Q is the larger of those sine values. The corresponding ambient C and S act blockwise, recording the full list rather than only the maximum.
slides.takeaway: The operator norm remembers the largest angle; the operators remember every angle.

slides.title: Rebuild the identities
slides.lead: The construction can be checked without naming a principal-angle basis.
body: Start from P²=P, Q²=Q and expand (P−Q)². Prove that this square commutes with each projection. Then define its positive square root and the complementary positive root.
Verify S²+C²=I and examine common, crossed, and generic directions. These computations are the algebraic core behind more advanced direct-rotation constructions.
slides.takeaway: Projection algebra plus positive square roots gives the full operator-trigonometric package.
